source.title: SoK: Unintended Interactions among Machine Learning Defenses and Risks
source.authors: Vasisht Duddu; Sebastian Szyller; N. Asokan

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses overfitting, memorization, and generalization, but it does not test any of the listed claim versions. Its experiments concern unintended interactions between ML defenses and risks.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for random-label memorization and discusses model capacity and overfitting, but those cited findings are not its own results. Its own toy-network illustration reports four train-test accuracy gaps; these do not test any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern constructed memorization–overfitting cases and defense–risk interactions. They do not test any listed version. The toy cases lack random-label versus natural-label training comparisons; the capacity experiment measures distribution-inference attacks, not improving held-out classification with width.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conjecture that overfitting and memorization underlie unintended defense–risk interactions, propose a framework and guideline, and empirically validate two conjectured interactions. They explicitly leave completeness open and qualify the framework as correlational rather than causal.
record.recipe_differences: The paper surveys prior work and proposes a framework for unintended interactions; its toy illustration is not a test of the listed generalization claims.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports generalization gaps of 0.00, 0.18, 0.00, and 0.16, with average memorization scores of 0.00, 0.00, 0.14, and 0.11, respectively, across four deliberately constructed synthetic cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this synthetic illustration, label-only memorization and a train–test accuracy gap can occur separately or together.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 reports increasing distribution-inference attack success across four larger MLP architectures, while classification accuracy remains 82.10 ± 1.17% and training accuracy is nearly perfect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger classifiers can leak more distribution information through explanations despite similar classification accuracy and generalization gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2024
record.problems: The generalization illustration is synthetic and uses a simple two-hidden-layer network; it does not test the listed claim versions. The paper describes its broader framework as based on prior work and notes that its interactions are correlational.
record.rows_left_out: No other results retained. The defense-risk experiments and cited prior findings do not test any listed claim version or directly measure its specified behavior.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, their training fits, and held-out accuracy relative to chance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove penalties.
Dropout's effects on held-out classification error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The original-source findings discussed in the survey are not this study's results. Figure 1's memorization scores supplement its illustration but do not create a test of a listed version. The defense–risk experiments were declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing claim-relevant rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Comparisons of convolutional and fully connected architectures on images.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparisons and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons against generalization gaps.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.
